transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Omar Santos (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Helix Head of ML), Tom Reed (Helix Infra), Priya Nair (Helix Product), Samir Kahn (Helix SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping call to align on integration approach for Helix's search+insights product. Focus: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and integration details (SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool-calling and structured outputs).

Topics:
- POC goals & success criteria
- Workload profile & sizing (throughput, latency targets)
- Benchmarks: what to run and how to measure cost/latency/quality
- Integration options: Redwood SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, JSON schema/structured output
- Timeline and next steps

Action items (recap in call end): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes. I'm Maya from Redwood, Daniel and Omar are with me on the SE side. Could folks quickly intro?
[00:12] Aisha Gomez: Hi I'm Aisha, Head of ML at Helix, we run a hybrid analytics product, so low-latency search is important.
[00:18] Tom Reed: Tom infra, responsible for cloud infra and our VPC networking.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Priya, product owner for search and insights.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today is to scope a POC — confirm success criteria, get workload sizing, agree benchmark runs, and align on integration path. We typically offer two integration styles: OpenAI-compatible endpoints for minimal changes, or our SDKs if you want built-in batching, caching and structured tool-calls.
[00:42] Daniel Park: Yeah, and from an SE perspective we want to nail the latency SLO you care about, token cost targets, and whether you need VPC/private deployment for data residency.
[00:52] Aisha Gomez: Success criteria from our side: 1) latency p95 under 250ms for short queries (<256 tokens) in the production topology; 2) quality parity with our current finetuned model for reranking and answer synthesis measured by our internal eval set; 3) predictable cost per 1M tokens under $1200 — that last one is negotiable but helps scope.
[01:15] Daniel Park: Okay p95 250ms is tight but doable on Dedicated or tuned hosted variants assuming batching is limited. One note — short queries don't benefit from large batch windows, so we'll configure low-latency batching.
[01:28] Tom Reed: Clarify dedicated vs hosted: our security team favors private deployment in our cloud account or a VPC peered option. We need audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration.
[01:41] Omar Santos: We support Private (VPC) with a private control plane — we can integrate with your KMS and provide audit logs and RBAC. There can be minor infra setup for peering, and we have a standard SAML integration guide.
[01:52] Priya Nair: On integration, we already talk to OpenAI endpoints for embeddings and completions. Ideally we want minimal code changes — OpenAI-compatible endpoints would be ideal. But we also want structured outputs and function calling for tool integrations.
[02:08] Daniel Park: Good — Redwood exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus native SDKs in Python/Node. The OpenAI-compatible path is a drop-in for your existing calls; our SDKs add features like automatic batching, prefix/K-V cahce (sic), and built-in structured JSON schema enforcement for outputs.
[02:25] Aisha Gomez: When you say function/tool calling, is that the same as OpenAI functions?
[02:29] Daniel Park: It's similar — we support function calling patterns. We also surface explicit tool integrations (e.g., DB lookups, vector search calls) and you can route tool calls through Webhooks or internal microservices. Note sometimes the transcript says "function calling" and the semantics may vary but it's compatible for typical patterns.
[02:45] Tom Reed: For benchmarks, what do you need from us?
[02:48] Maya Chen: We need a representative traffic trace if possible: request sizes, concurrency, percentiles, and an eval set for quality measurement. Ideally sample of 500–2,000 queries for the eval. Also tell us peak qps and typical session patterns.
[03:02] Samir Kahn: We can provide a 7-day trace and a 1k eval set. Our peak is around 120 rps now, but that includes embeddings batch jobs; for the realtime search path it's closer to 40 rps with spikes up to 80.
[03:15] Daniel Park: That helps. For benchmarks we'll run three profiles: single-request latency (no batching), steady-state throughput with realistic concurrency, and quality eval against your labeled set. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and error rates. We'll also run model variant fallbacks to test graceful degradation.
[03:33] Priya Nair: How do we instrument results into our dashboards? We use Datadog.
[03:37] Omar Santos: We can push metrics via Prometheus/Datadog exporters, and provide trace hooks. Redwood Console also exports per-route breakdowns that you can ingest.
[03:45] Aisha Gomez: On the integration side, sample code is critical. What will you share?
[03:49] Daniel Park: We'll share a short integration repo with Python and Node examples using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and our SDK. It includes: 1) completions/generation example; 2) function calling example (tool invocation flow); 3) structured JSON schema enforcement and validation snippets; 4) examples showing how to enable prefix caching and batching for lower cost. We'll also include a demo of streaming responses.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Streaming is important for UX. Also we need structured outputs for downstream parsers — we use JSON schema validation today.
[04:23] Daniel Park: We support structured outputs via schema hints in the request and validation hooks in the SDK. Small caveat: schema enforcement sometimes needs iteration — we'd recommend a short loop during POC to stabilize output shapes.
[04:34] Tom Reed: Networking/peering notes: our security team requires TLS mutual auth for peering and we need SLA info.
[04:40] Omar Santos: We have mTLS options for Private deployments and an SLA document which Maya will attach. Also our security pack includes SOC2 docs and the KMS integration steps.
[04:50] Aisha Gomez: What's the estimated timeline for the POC?
[04:53] Maya Chen: Proposal sent within a few days, then infra setup 1 week after sign-off, benchmark runs 1–2 weeks, quality eval and iteration 1 week, and a final review. So end-to-end ~4–6 weeks depending on infra windows.
[05:07] Samir Kahn: That sounds reasonable. We will need a test window for peering at the beginning of week of 2025-10-13 — we can tentatively block that.
[05:16] Daniel Park: For SDKs, quick note: OpenAI-compatible endpoints accept identical request/response shapes but Redwood adds headers for routing and additional query params for model variants. We'll provide a migration doc.
[05:28] Priya Nair: Any limits on function calling or tool integrations we should know about?
[05:31] Daniel Park: No hard limits, but for high qps we recommend using lightweight local tool invocation or queueing to avoid blocking the runtime. Also watch KV cache size for long-context sessions — we can recommend quantization or variant models for longer contexts.
[05:46] Aisha Gomez: On cost: can you provide an estimate for our workload?
[05:49] Maya Chen: Yes — once you send the sample traces and eval set we'll run a cost projection for the candidate model variants. We'll include dedicated vs hosted comparisons and the impact of batching and KV caching.
[06:01] Tom Reed: Ok, security review will want the SOC2, ISO docs, and details on audit log retention.
[06:06] Omar Santos: We'll share the security pack and our compliance contacts.
[06:10] Priya Nair: Any blockers from a product side?
[06:12] Priya Nair: Main thing is making sure function-calling behaves identical to our current system — small differences in argument ordering caused failures previously.
[06:19] Daniel Park: We'll include a function-calling smoke test in the integration repo and a checklist for argument shapes and retries.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Great. Recap next steps — Daniel will share the integration guide and SDK snippets by 2025-10-04. Maya will send the POC proposal + pricing by 2025-10-06. Helix provides traces and eval by 2025-10-09. We tentatively schedule infra peering and a benchmark week starting 2025-10-13.
[06:45] Aisha Gomez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:49] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links — we'll include our shared deck (/s/Helix-POC-deck) and security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security-pack).
[06:58] End of meeting.
